chapter_name: The Price Puzzle: What Drives the Market
learning_objective: 🎯 Explore how the invisible forces of Supply and Demand interact to determine the prices of everything we buy!

key_vocabulary.hindi_meaning: लोच (कीमत बदलने पर मांग में बदलाव)

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Generally, when the price of a good goes UP, the quantity demanded by consumers goes DOWN (and vice versa). People buy less of expensive things.
Generally, when the price of a good goes UP, the quantity supplied by producers goes UP. Businesses want to sell more when prices are high to make a bigger profit.
The 'magic point' where the quantity consumers want to buy exactly equals the quantity producers want to sell. This crossing point determines the final market price.
If the price is set too low, demand exceeds supply, causing a Shortage. If the price is set too high, supply exceeds demand, causing a Surplus (leftover stock).
How sensitive consumers are to a price change. 'Inelastic' goods (like medicines) are bought even if prices rise. 'Elastic' goods (like luxury watches) see a big drop in demand if prices rise.

fun_activity.title: 🍋 The Lemonade Stand
fun_activity.instructions: Imagine you sell lemonade. If you charge ₹10, you sell 50 cups. If you charge ₹50, you only sell 5 cups. Draw a simple downward-sloping line on a graph to show your 'Demand Curve'!

exam_tips: 📌 Always remember the inverse relationship for Demand (Price ↑ Demand ↓) and the direct relationship for Supply (Price ↑ Supply ↑).
📌 Equilibrium is achieved without government interference; it is guided by the 'Invisible Hand' of the market.
📌 Be able to list factors other than price that change demand (e.g., income, trends, substitute goods).
quick_recap: ⭐ A market is not necessarily a physical place; it is any arrangement where buyers and sellers interact.
⭐ When demand increases (like umbrellas in the rain), the price usually goes up.
⭐ Essential goods have inelastic demand because people cannot easily stop buying them.
